stories.headline: Chicago's Whole Wagon Train Threw a Wheel in One Afternoon
stories.read: Hold up there, pardner, this is the ugliest news on the Trail today. D'Andre Swift limped off late in Thursday's practice with a bad left leg, and Rome Odunze went down early clutchin' a right leg, and neither fella had so much as sneezed all camp. Worse, the spare horse is already lame: backup Kyle Monangai is nursin' a knee and coach Ben Johnson called him week-to-week Tuesday. So a top-shelf offense heads into the opener with its runner, its number-two receiver, and its insurance policy all questionable at once. Push Swift and Odunze down your board a hair, and go stake a claim on whoever's third in that pecking order before the saloon reads the same wire you just did.

stories.headline: Coin Flip in the Desert: Jeremiyah Love Is 50/50, and Allgeier Is Cheap Gold
stories.read: Word from the wire says the Cardinals rookie is about even money to suit up against the Chargers, still walkin' off a preseason high ankle sprain. If he sits, he'll likely be back by Week 2 or 3, so nobody oughta be dumpin' him. Here's the play though: Tyler Allgeier is sittin' out there on the open range with a bell-cow's share of the reins waitin' on him if Love can't go. That's a free lottery ticket for the price of a late-round dart. Grab Allgeier as the spare horse, ride him Week 1, and thank me from up on Championship Mesa.

stories.headline: Atlanta's Still Squintin' at Two Quarterbacks With the Sun Comin' Up
stories.read: Five days from kickoff and the Falcons are the last outfit in the league without a named triggerman, still weighin' Michael Penix Jr., who only just got cleared full-go off that torn knee, against Tua Tagovailoa. That fog is doin' real damage to Drake London's price, and a nervous outfit will let a true alpha receiver slide a round he don't deserve. Doesn't much matter who wins it, pardner, somebody's throwin' him the ball and Bijan's still gettin' the reins twenty times a Sunday. Buy the confusion. Diamonds get cheap when the herd can't see three feet ahead.
